messages:
Nina: Quick postmortem from todays geo test: several EU-locked tenants saw read errors during a regional spike. Root cause: residency decision performed after KV auth. We should discuss short-circuiting that check.

Omar: agreed. Short-term fix: maintain a tiny residency LRU in the edge proxy populated from control-plane deltas. Avoids auth/KV work for obvious decisions.

Priya: compliance reminder: tenants marked `blocked_residency` cannot be served outside their region. No opt-in. Any cross-region decision must emit an audit record with provenance.

Theo: ops angle: if we allow opt-in fallbacks, gate them at the proxy with steady+burst + a global circuit-breaker based on remote CPU ratio. Also surface in Console when fallbacks are limited.

Nina: prototype numbers from a 2h sim: baseline errors 2.7% -> with proxy short-circuit 0.4% and auth CPU reduced 11%.

Omar: implementation note: control-plane will expose a /v1/tenants/:id/residency and a delta push websocket. Proxies subscribe and maintain a small in-memory map plus TTL.

Priya: add consent_type to policy (ui|support|legal) and require audit id. Also, writes must never fallback without explicit contract clause.

compliance-bot: audit-rule-created: rule=residency-fallback-v1, required_fields=[consent_type,compliance_id,audit_stream].

Nina: action items: Omar spike websocket + LRU; Theo simulate thresholds and console indicator; Priya draft compliance checklist. I'll draft RFC follow-up with rollout plan (10% tenants -> 50% -> full opt-in).

Theo: quick question: do we want a priming probe when fallback first occurs? It helps cold-starts but adds extra load. Suggest priming with low priority and short TTL.

Omar: yeah, priming helps. Make it optional per-policy with prime_ttl_s. We'll include in policy JSON in RFC.

Nina: thanks all, will post RFC soon.
